item.title: Comment on Malaria Symptoms and Causes by Charlotte
item.description: In reply to <a href="https://www.malaria.com/overview/malaria-symptoms-causes#comment-284">Yvonne</a>. This is exactly the case with me. I have not recovered since I had malaria P. falciparium a year ago. My memory is terrible, I have no energy, I have pain in my body, (mainly legs) and I agree with the sweating and recently I was informed that I have hit early menopause. Research I have done shows that is can be caused in rare cases by malaria. Doctors however are finding it difficult to figure

item.title: Comment on Long term health effects of malaria when young? by Jemima Walsh
item.description: I was relieved to see similar symptoms described by people on this forum. I have suffered inexplicable fatigue and ill health in adulthood including fybromyalgia, signs of minor liver damage and gastric intolerances. I contracted malaria as a toddler in PNG in the 1970s. I recall having several febrile hallucinations as a teenager in Australia which is malaria-free. Again despite the lack of clinical evidence I am certain of a link. I recently gave blood and screening showed malarial antibodies.

item.title: Comment on Long and Short Term Effects of Malaria by B. Joseph
item.description: I too had malaria while in Vietnam 1967-1968. I was hospitalized for about 10 days. After that, my whole life, I experienced night sweats and on numerous occasions, dizziness. I have also found that I may have liver problems - tests are still ungoing for that.

item.title: Comment on Long and Short Term Effects of Malaria by Rodell
item.description: I am surprised that at the claim of no long term effects: my father caught malaria serving in Africa and the India during the second world war, the after effects of night and day sweats remained with him for years.
